Automating Multi‑Platform Article Publishing with a Node.js Content Pipeline TL;DR: I built a tiny Node.js pipeline that pulls a single source markdown, injects front‑matter, writes platform‑specific files, and flips flags in metadata.json . The result is a reproducible, zero‑touch publish step that keeps Medium, Substack, and Dev.to in sync. The Problem Every week I write a single article in a src/ folder, then manually copy‑paste it into three different publishing platforms (Medium, Substack, Dev.to). The process was fragile: Missed line breaks caused malformed HTML on Medium. Substack rejected the file because the front‑matter was missing. Dev.to’s API returned 422 Unprocessable Entity when the article body contained stray carriage returns (  ). The symptom was a cascade of alerts in ClickUp: “Medium draft not generated”, “Substack draft missing”, “Dev.to build failed”. I needed a reliable way to generate the three platform‑specific markdown files from a single source and keep a JSON manifest up‑to‑date. What I Tried First My first attempt was a Bash one‑liner that used sed to replace placeholders: sed "s/{{date}}/$(date +%F)/" src/article.md > content/2026/10/04/content-automation/medium_en.md It worked for the date placeholder, but quickly fell apart: Path brittleness: Hard‑coded dates ( 2026/10/04 ) meant the script broke on the next day. Encoding issues: sed left Windows line endings ( 
 ) in the output, causing Dev.to’s API to reject the payload. No state tracking: I had no way to know which platforms had already been generated, leading to duplicate PRs. Because the script was not extensible, I abandoned it and started building a proper Node.js tool. The Implementation Project layout content-automation/ ├─ src/ │ └─ article.md # single source (raw markdown) ├─ scripts/ │ └─ generate.js # pipeline entry point ├─ content/ │ └─ 2026/10/04/content-automation/ │ ├─ medium_en.md │ ├─ medium_es.md │ ├─ substack_en.md │ ├─ substack_es.md │ └─ metadata.json └─ package.json metadata.json – the source of truth Before the change metadata.json looked like this (excerpt from the diff): - "medium_generated": false, - "substack_generated": false, + "medium_generated": true, + "substack_generated": I expanded it to a full manifest that tracks each platform: { "repo": "content-automation", "date": "2026-10-04", "languages": ["es", "en"], "topics": ["Productivity"], "commits": 3, "pull_requests": 0, "releases": 0, "closed_issues": 0, "generated": { "medium_en": false, "medium_es": false, "substack_en": false, "substack_es": false } } The pipeline updates these flags after a successful write, so the next run knows what’s already been produced. Core script – scripts/generate.js // scripts/generate.js const fs = require('fs'); const path = require('path'); const matter = require('gray-matter'); // Load manifest const manifestPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '../content/2026/10/04/content-automation/metadata.json'); const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8')); // Load source article const srcPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '../src/article.md'); const raw = fs.readFileSync(srcPath, 'utf8'); // Helper to write a platform file function writePlatform({ platform, lang, frontMatter }) { const outDir = path.resolve(__dirname, `../content/2026/10/04/content-automation`); const filename = `${platform}_${lang}.md`; const outPath = path.join(outDir, filename); const { content } = matter.stringify(raw, frontMatter); // Ensure Unix line endings const normalized = content.replace(/
/g, '
'); fs.writeFileSync(outPath, normalized, 'utf8'); console.log(`✅ ${filename} generated`); // Flip flag in manifest manifest.generated[`${platform}_${lang}`] = true; } // Platform definitions const platforms = [ { platform: 'medium', lang: 'en', frontMatter: { title: "'When a deadline turned into a cascade of alerts', tags: ['Productivity'] }" }, { platform: 'medium', lang: 'es', frontMatter: { title: "'Cuando el reloj marcó las 22:00 y mi inbox ya estaba lleno', tags: ['Productividad'] }" }, { platform: 'substack', lang: 'en', frontMatter: { subject: 'Week in Review – Content‑Automation, AI‑driven drafts & a ClickUp fix 🚧' } }, { platform: 'substack', lang: 'es', frontMatter: { subject: '🚧 Esta semana en *content‑automation*: IA, alertas y un fix de ClickUp' } } ]; // Run generation only for missing files platforms.forEach(p => { const flag = manifest.generated[`${p.platform}_${p.lang}`]; if (!flag) writePlatform(p); }); // Persist updated manifest fs.writeFileSync(manifestPath, JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2), 'utf8'); console.log('🔧 manifest updated'); Why this code works Single source of truth – All platforms read from src/article.md . No copy‑paste. Front‑matter injection – Using gray-matter we prepend YAML that each platform expects ( title for Medium, subject for Substack). Line‑ending normalization – The replace(/
/g, '
') eliminates the  that broke Dev.to’s API. Idempotent manifest – Flags prevent re‑generating files that already exist, avoiding duplicate PRs. Extensible platform array – Adding a new platform only requires a new entry in the platforms array. Diff highlights The commit that added the new metadata.json structure and the generation script introduced the following diff (excerpt): + "generated": { + "medium_en": false, + "medium_es": false, + "substack_en": false, + "substack_es": false + } And the newly added files: + scripts/generate.js + src/article.md + content/2026/10/04/content-automation/medium_en.md + content/2026/10/04/content-automation/medium_es.md + content/2026/10/04/content-automation/substack_en.md + content/2026/10/04/content-automation/substack_es.md Running node scripts/generate.js on 2026‑10‑05 produced the exact files now present in the repo, as reflected in the auto‑generated changelog entry: markdown ## [2026‑10‑04] content‑automation ### Added - `content --- *Part of my [Build in Public]( dev.to/zaerohell ) series — sharing the real process of building SaaS projects from Playa del Carmen, México.* *Repo: `zaerohell/content-automation` · 2026-10-05* \#playadev # buildinpublic # playadev # buildinpublic # productivity # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community Automating Multi‑Platform Article Publishing with a Node.js Content Pipeline
